review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 23, 11:56 AM ET. It had Bobcats 34% and Bengals 66%, projecting Bobcats 1.4 – Bengals 2.1 (3.5 total, Bengals by 0.7).

Final: Bobcats 0 – Bengals 2. Right winner: it had Bengals at 66%.

review.body:
Bobcats came in with a 4% below average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 12 and 12 games of evidence. Projected to score 1.4, they scored 0 (−1.4 sets, 100% under); projected to allow 2.1, they allowed 2 (−0.1 sets, 4% under).

Bengals came in with a 15% above average attack and a 17% stingier than average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 12 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 2.1, they scored 2 (−0.1 sets, 4% under); projected to allow 1.4, they allowed 0 (−1.4 sets, 100% under).

The bigger miss was Bobcats' scoring (-1.4 sets against projection).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.611 of the raw projection. It counts toward Volleyball scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 725 graded Volleyball games the algo now scales scoring ×0.965 and gives home teams +0.2 sets. Team corrections so far: Bobcats attack ×0.960, defense ×0.968 (5 games); Bengals attack ×1.040, defense ×0.960 (5 games).

The tracker grades it from the final within a few minutes; then it joins the learning.
